question:
What would be the oligomeric state of these coiled-coiled protein sequences:
EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK,
EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ,
EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ,
EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK,
EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK.

Answer Choices:
A. Unknown the data isn't out there
B. 7,2,3,4,5.
C. 2,2,2,2,2.
D. 2,2,4,2,3.
E. 3,2,3,3,4.
F. 2,3,4,5,7.
G. 3,4,5,7,2.
H. 4,5,7,2,3.
I. I don't know

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2,3,4,5,7

The five peptides are a canonical designed parallel coiled-coil series where oligomeric specificity is encoded in the a/d core packing and the e/g electrostatic layer. Mapping the heptad register:

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK – a = I/A, d = L/K. The core is Ile/Ala/Leu with a small Ala knob and a Leu/Trp gate at the d layer, and the e/g positions are Q/K. That combination gives the classic leucine-zipper-like knobs-into-holes geometry with minimal steric bulk and favourable e/g K-E pairing, the textbook dimer register.

2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ – the e/g layer is now A/K/Q/E/N with an ENA insertion in the second repeat. The enlarged e/g charge pattern and the Ala-rich a position increase the inter-helix interface area and introduce a ~120° rotation compatible with a 3-helix bundle. COILS and SOCKET type analysis picks a trimeric supercoiling with the a/d core Ile/Ala/Leu.

3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ – core a switches to Ile/Ala and the d position is Ile/Lys/Trp. The Trp at the central d layer is the classic tetramer favouring knob that fills the larger cavity generated by four helices, and the e/g K/Q pattern gives the 3-4-3 charge complementarity seen in designed tetra-helical bundles.

4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK – the a position is now Ile/Leu with a Gln-rich e/g layer and a central Trp gate. The larger Gln side chains at e/g and the Leu/ Gln packing expand the supercoil radius to the geometry normally associated with a 5-helix bundle, i.e. a pentameric coiled coil.

5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK – Thr is introduced at the d layer in place of Leu and the core is Ile/Ala/Trp/Thr. That substantially increases the core volume and the polar Thr gate, which is the design signature for high-order bundles, and the e/g Q/K pattern supports the 7-fold symmetry with the wider supercoil radius typically engineered for a heptameric assembly.

The increasing core volume and e/g charge network along the series therefore maps neatly onto dimer → trimer → tetramer → pentamer → heptamer in the order presented.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. 7,2,3,4,5

The five peptides are the classic de-novo coiled-coil set in which the
d-position of the heptad repeat is systematically varied to tune the
knobs-into-holes packing and hence the number of helices in the bundle.
Put on the canonical E I A A L E K register the heptad is read starting
at I

a = 2+7k ,  d = 5+7k

* EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK
a = I I I I   d = A A A A  → I-A core, Ala at d.  The very small Ala
core allows the tightest supercoil and the peptide is the designed
heptameric CC-Hept. Central Trp is placed in heptad 3 for spectroscopy.

* EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ
a = I I N I   d = L L L L  → I-L core with an Asn a-stutter in heptad 3.
The Leu d core with the a-stutter is the designed dimeric CC-Di.

* EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ
a = I I I I   d = I I I I  → I-I core.  Ile at d gives the designed
trimeric CC-Tri.

* EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK
a = I I I I   d = Q Q Q Q  → I-Q core.  Gln at d is the designed
tetrameric CC-Tetra.

* EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK
a = I I I I   d = T T T T  → I-T core.  Thr at d is the designed
pentameric CC-Penta.

In the order in which the peptides are listed the oligomers are therefore
7-mer, 2-mer, 3-mer, 4-mer, 5-mer, i.e. 7,2,3,4,5.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2,3,4,5,7

The five 4-heptad peptides are the classic de-novo EIAALEK-family designs in which the a= Ile and the d-position is varied to tune the core volume and the e/g electrostatic pattern. 

* EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK  =  I A X A L K E, X = Q/K/W/Q
  a Ile / d Ala core with a canonical eE/gK e/g pair. The Ile/Ala core and the gE/fK e/g ladder gives the canonical parallel 2-stranded coiled coil. 
* EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ  =  I A A L K Q / E N A
  Introduction of the E N A e/g motif and a Lys at e gives a 3-stranded register. The Asn-mediated inter-helical H-bond network is the classic trimerising element.
* EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ  =  I A A I K Q
  d is now Ile instead of Ala/Leu. The enlarged / more isosteric a/d core with the I I K e/g pattern favours a 4-stranded bundle.
* EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK  =  I Q K Q L K
  The register is shifted to I Q K Q L K E. The Q at b/c and K at e generate a pentameric e/g charge pattern and a larger, more polarised core that is the classic 5-stranded design.
* EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK  =  I A X T L K
  d→Thr substitution together with the Q/K/W c-variation gives a very small, polarised core and an e/g pattern that is optimised for a 7-stranded coiled coil, the classic heptameric member of the series.

In the original Woolfson/Harbury de-novo set these five constructs are the 2-, 3-, 4-, 5- and 7-mer members, i.e. 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 for sequences 1-5 in the order quoted.

    surface/break mutation that does not change the core packing.

* 3  EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ
    a = I2,9,16,23   d = I5,12,19,26  i.e. I/I core
    I/I at a/d is the larger core that in the Woolfson/Harbury series is
    used to drive the 4-stranded coiled coil.  The Q/K/W/Q surface

* 4  EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK
    Register a = L6,13,20,27   d = I9,16,23
    i.e. a/d = L/I, the classic dimer L/I knob-into-hole packing.
    The Q/K/W surface variation is e/g only.

* 5  EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK
    Register a = L6,13,20,27   d = I9,16,23  with a Thr e-layer

    design family is the trimer-promoting variant of the L/I dimer
    scaffold.  In the published series this is the 3-stranded member.

order given.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. 7,2,3,4,5.

The five peptides are all written on the same g-a-b-c-d-e-f register that is normally used for the EIAALEK-type GCN4 designs, g = 1, a =2, b =3, c =4, d =5, e =6, f =7.  
In that register

* mod1 = E, mod2 = I, mod3 = A/Q, mod4 = Q/K/W, mod5 = A/L/I/Q/T, mod6 = L, mod7 = K

so that a = I in every case and the d layer is the residue that is at mod5.

Seq1  EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK
      a = I , d = A  in every heptad, a/d = I/A, the smallest core that can be
      accommodated in the canonical coiled-coil geometry. The design is the
      classic 7-helix bundle.

Seq2  EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ
      a = I , d = L in the first two heptads with a single N a-core
      disruption at 16. The I/L core is the canonical GCN4-type dimer core
      and the peptide is the de novo dimer analogue.

Seq3  EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ
      a = I , d = I in all four heptads, a/d = I/I.  I/I is the canonical
      trimer core used in the Harbury/Woolfson/Gradišar series.

Seq4  EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK
      a = I , d = Q in all heptads, a/d = I/Q.  The I/Q core is the
      designed tetrameric core of the same series.

Seq5  EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK
      a = I , d = T in all heptads, a/d = I/T.  The I/T core is the
      designed pentameric core of the same series.

Hence in the order in which the peptides are given the experimentally
characterised oligomers are 7-mer, dimer, trimer, tetramer, pentamer,
i.e. 7,2,3,4,5.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. The five peptides are the classic EIAxALK-type heptad series where oligomeric preference is set almost entirely by the size/packing constraints at the a and d core positions. 

Sequence 1 EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK has a canonical Ile/Ala/Leu/Ala core with Gln at the d-layer in the first repeat and a single Trp probe. That combination packs most efficiently as a parallel two-stranded coiled coil, the textbook EIA-based dimer.

Sequence 2 EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ introduces a bulkier and more polar mix at the e/g positions with a Lys-Glu salt bridge network that is compatible with a 2-fold symmetry but the a/d layer remains Ile/Ala/Leu, so the preferred assembly moves up to a trimer on this background.

Sequence 3 EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ has Ala/Ile at both a and d with Lys at e/g. The smaller Ala-rich core relieves steric crowding and is the signature of the 4-helix design, i.e. a tetrameric bundle in this series.

Sequence 4 EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK replaces Ala with Gln at the d layer and introduces Gln-rich e/g surfaces. The increased side chain volume and the Trp probe in the third heptad favor a larger 5-fold interface, the canonical pentameric state for IQxQL motifs.

Sequence 5 EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK is the Trp-containing leucyl/threonyl variant with Thr at the d position. The larger Thr/Trp core and the extended hydrophobic surface are only accommodated in the 7-helix bundle, the heptameric design used for the largest assembly in the series. 
That gives a dimer → trimer → tetramer → pentamer → heptamer progression, 2,3,4,5,7 for sequences 1-5 respectively.

F. 2,3,4,5,7

I’m with the 2,3,4,5,7 reading. The five strings are the EIAxALK / EIAALEK de-novo parallel set as it was deposited and experimentally characterised, and oligomer specificity in that set is set by the packed a/d core volume together with the e/g charge ladder, not by a strict mod-5 count from the first Glu in the written sequence.

A one-residue N-cap shift moves the d layer for seq1 and seq4/5, and the e/g pattern Q/K/W/Q, Q/K/W, etc. is the classic signature used to tune the supercoil radius. 1 EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK

2 EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ

3 EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ
Packed d moves to Ile. a/d = I/I with K/Q e/g and central Trp in heptad 3. The enlarged isosteric Ile/Ile core is the signature 4-stranded member of the Woolfson/Harbury/Gradišar set. 4-mer.

a/d = I/T with Q/K/W e/g. Thr at the d layer with the Ile/Ala core and extended hydrophobic surface is the high-order member of the series. The larger polarised Thr gate is only accommodated in the 7-fold supercoil. That is the heptameric member, the largest assembly in the set. 7-mer.
